chapter: Moving to California and the war years
title: The decline and death of Leo Watson
summary: After the Spirits broke up around 1943 Leo drank wine downtown and died there, though he recorded with Vic Dickenson and Artie Shaw.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I'm trying to -- still trying to get back to after the Spirits finally broke up, you know, when did -- when did you last see Leo?
What did he do? The Spirits broke up around '42.
Was he just working a day job?
No. Leo was downtown. He was downtown just goofing.

Drinking that wine. And that's what he died of, that wine, laying in them places, and on the streets, you know. He'd be laying down and the guys would pick him up for the night, he'd get some sleep, and then he would -- they'd let him out in the morning, and he'd go right back to that wine. God rest his soul.
The greatest man I've known in years, Leo was. I mean, anything he'd hear, he'd play.
Why couldn't -- why couldn't he get it together, you know, what was the problem there?
But he could have got with another group, or something like that.
Leo was with what's-his-name. He was with -- wow.
He made some records with Vic Dickenson.
And he made some with -- what's that boy's name, that got a band, come out here and played clarinet?
He was with Artie Shaw's band.
Oh, yeah? What, around -- after the Spirits broke up?
Uh-huh. He come out here with them.
So he had some opportunity there.
He came out here with them.
